prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Warehouse system boundary: from receiving interface to release of completed outbound load at shipping interface. Pallets stay inside while inspected, identified, buffered, stored, retrieved, prepared for dispatch. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk (records inspection outcomes before accepted pallets enter storage); Pallet Dimension Scanner (captures dimensions for handling/storage eligibility); Inbound Pallet Buffer (temporarily holds accepted pallets when storage cannot proceed); North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane (storage/retrieval in designated aisles); East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor (carry pallets on designated routes); Conveyor Line Controller (coordinates conveyor movement); Autonomous Forklift Fleet (moves pallets only in approved travel areas under authorized tasking); Yard Gate Controller (vehicle access at perimeter); Outbound Dispatch Sorter (sequences eligible pallets for dispatch); Outbound Checkweigh Scale (verifies pallet weight before shipment completion); Shipping Documentation Desk (prepares outbound load records); Safety Zone Controller (enforces movement restrictions in protected areas); Fire Alarm Panel (provides alarm status); Maintenance Release Terminal (records equipment availability). Actor: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery decisions). Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authority for inventory records and release of warehouse work; maintains authoritative pallet status, location, handling eligibility. Requirements: inbound acceptance requires valid receipt instruction and safely handleable pallet; inbound arrivals checked against scheduled delivery window before door assignment; storage locations assigned for safe handling, efficient retrieval, inventory controls; no equipment may begin inventory-moving work without authorized release from Warehouse Management System; physical movement and system inventory status must be reconciled; objective: process accepted pallets accurately, meet committed dispatch times without bypassing safety or inventory controls.

New part:
S028: The Yard Gate Controller records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, and arrival time.
S029: Yard Gate Controller is also known as Velvetrook.
S030: Drivers follow the gate instructions to the designated staging lane while a receiving door is prepared.
S031: The gate process flags unscheduled arrivals for review before they enter the receiving area.
S032: The Inbound Inspection Desk is also known as Cinderbay.
S033: The Inbound Inspection Desk checks delivery paperwork against the expected shipment and confirms the trailer is presented for inspection.
S034: Staff verify trailer identification and inspect accessible seals before unloading is authorized.
S035: Visible damage, mismatched identifiers, or compromised seals are recorded with the affected shipment details.
S036: The Inbound Inspection Desk sends the Trailer Seal Exception Note when a seal discrepancy requires follow-up.
S037: A receiving door is assigned only when the door, staging lane, and unloading crew are available.
S038: Door assignments are coordinated with the current yard position so that trailers do not obstruct active traffic routes.
S039: The Yard Gate Controller directs each cleared trailer from staging to its assigned receiving door.
S040: If a door becomes unavailable, the trailer remains in a safe holding position until a revised assignment is confirmed.
S041: The Warehouse Management System maintains the expected inbound shipment data used during receiving checks.
S042: The Warehouse Management System sends the Dispatch Wave Amendment when outbound planning requires a change.
S043: Receiving staff compare the physical pallet count with the shipment paperwork before unloading is completed.
S044: Pallets with visible damage are kept separate from acceptable stock while the discrepancy is assessed.
S045: The Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection results promptly so warehouse inventory remains aligned with the received goods.
S046: Door occupancy and clearance are monitored throughout unloading to prevent conflicting vehicle movements.
S047: Yard personnel notify receiving staff when a trailer is ready to leave the door and return to the yard route.
S048: Unloading is paused if an unsafe condition, documentation conflict, or equipment issue is discovered.
S049: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor resolves receiving issues that exceed the desk's routine authority.
S050: The receiving process closes after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release are recorded.
S051: Storage allocation begins after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release have been recorded.
S052: The Warehouse Management System evaluates available positions against pallet dimensions, mass, storage compatibility, and expected retrieval demand.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response: {"summary":"Warehouse boundary: receiving interface to release of outbound load at shipping interface. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork vs expected shipment, verifies trailer ID/seals, records damage/mismatches/seal issues and inspection results promptly; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note on seal discrepancy); Pallet Dimension Scanner (dimensions for eligibility); Inbound Pallet Buffer; North and South Aisle Stacker Cranes; East and West Transfer Conveyors; Conveyor Line Controller; Autonomous Forklift Fleet (approved areas, authorized tasks); Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (vehicle access; records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, arrival time; flags unscheduled arrivals for review; directs drivers to staging lane, then cleared trailers to assigned receiving door); Outbound Dispatch Sorter; Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk; Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel; Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery; resolves receiving issues beyond desk authority); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel (notify when trailer ready to leave door). Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: inventory authority, releases work; holds pallet status/location/eligibility and expected inbound shipment data; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment on outbound plan change; allocates storage by dimensions, mass, compatibility, retrieval demand. Requirements: inbound acceptance needs valid receipt instruction and handleable pallet; arrivals checked against delivery window before door assignment; seals/trailer ID verified before unloading authorized; door assigned only when door, staging lane, crew available, coordinated with yard position to avoid blocking traffic; if door unavailable, trailer holds safely until revised assignment; pallet count compared to paperwork before unloading completes; damaged pallets segregated; door occupancy monitored; unloading paused on unsafe condition, documentation conflict or equipment issue; receiving closes after count, inspection status, door release recorded, then storage allocation begins; no inventory-moving work without WMS release; physical and system status reconciled; meet dispatch times without bypassing safety/inventory controls."}
